problem: Understanding how Rademacher complexity, a fundamental measure of function class size used for generalization bounds, contracts under composition is unclear for sequential and offset variants used in online and squared-loss learning.
approach: Extends the classical Ledoux-Talagrand contraction lemma to sequential and offset Rademacher complexities, proving contraction holds under structural assumptions at the cost of polylogarithmic factors, and shows these factors cannot be removed generally.
contribution: Establishes that sequential and offset Rademacher complexities exhibit fundamentally different contraction behavior than classical Rademacher complexity, with tight characterization of when contraction is possible and its sample complexity costs.

problem: Brain-Computer Interfaces are limited by specialized single-task models that ignore inter-task synergies and cannot flexibly handle multiple encoding and decoding tasks.
approach: Proposes Mind-Omni, a unified framework using a novel Brain Tokenizer to convert continuous brain signals into discrete tokens, enabling multi-modal interactions via discrete diffusion and incorporating a Brain Question Answering dataset for reasoning.
contribution: Establishes a new multi-task unified framework for brain-vision-language modeling that achieves competitive or superior performance to larger specialized models while demonstrating multi-task synergy.

problem: Semi-supervised referring expression segmentation suffers from limited labeled data and unreliable pseudo-labels when exploiting unlabeled image-text pairs.
approach: Introduces Learning to Label, a reinforced self-evolving framework that leverages a multimodal LLM to extract semantic-spatial priors, formulates pseudo-label construction as learnable decision-making, and uses reinforced selection to adaptively reward high-utility pixel supervision.
contribution: Demonstrates improved semi-supervised referring expression segmentation on RefCOCO variants through joint optimization of segmentation model and pseudo-labels under sparse supervision.

problem: In-context learning for nonparametric regression requires understanding how transformers can achieve minimax optimal rates with practical parameter and pretraining requirements.
approach: Proves transformers with Θ(log n) parameters can achieve minimax optimal convergence rates O(n^{-2α/(2α+d)}) by implementing kernel-weighted polynomial basis and gradient descent with Ω(n^{2α/(2α+d)}log³ n) pretraining sequences.
contribution: Shows transformers can efficiently approximate local polynomial estimators for Hölder-smooth nonparametric regression with substantially fewer parameters and pretraining sequences than prior results.

problem: Computing U-statistics with kernel functions of degree k≥2 in federated learning under privacy guarantees remains challenging, with existing methods providing poor utility or scaling poorly.
approach: Proposes a protocol leveraging Multi-Party Computation to securely compute U-statistics under central differential privacy, providing detailed theoretical analysis of accuracy, communication, and computational properties.
contribution: Substantially improves accuracy for private federated U-statistics computation, achieving up to four orders of magnitude MSE reduction over existing baselines for statistics like Kendall's τ coefficient.

problem: Cross-subject emotion recognition is limited by heavy dependence on modality-specific feature designs and the unrealistic assumption of independently and identically distributed data.
approach: Introduces MixEmo framework that analyzes heterogeneous distribution characteristics, uses well-trained backbones to extract representations partitioned into distribution prototypes, randomly combines them to synthesize unseen distributions, and applies collaborative learning.
contribution: Substantially improves cross-subject emotion recognition generalization through heterogeneous distribution augmentation and collaborative learning without requiring modality-specific designs.

problem: Deploying large language models as high-level coordinators for multi-agent cooperation is challenging because effective policies often fail at low-level control and inference costs limit scalability.
approach: Proposes SynCoord, a self-supervised pipeline that distills task-level coordination from LLMs into lightweight agent policies using task-level tool interfaces to constrain LLM interaction and collect training trajectories.
contribution: Achieves comparable success rates and execution efficiency to RL methods while generalizing to unseen team compositions and larger layouts without retraining, reducing inference overhead.

problem: Multimodal LLMs remain brittle on mechanical engineering drawings due to high annotation density, weak domain knowledge, and unreliable spatial relation reasoning under projection rules.
approach: Introduces MechVQA, a comprehensive mechanical drawing understanding dataset with 21K question-answer pairs across three capability levels, and develops MechVL model through multi-stage training to specialize in mechanical drawings.
contribution: Outperforms strongest baseline by 7.57 percentage points on MechVQA, establishing domain-specialized foundation for deploying MLLMs in mechanical design and inspection.

problem: Reinforcement learning for diffusion models lacks systematic understanding of how likelihood estimation methods affect RL performance, with existing approaches relying on ad hoc estimators.
approach: Systematically analyzes RL design space by disentangling policy-gradient objectives, likelihood estimators, and rollout schemes, showing ELBO-based likelihood estimation from final samples dominates performance.
contribution: Improves GenEval score from 0.24 to 0.95 in 90 GPU hours, achieving 4.6× efficiency over FlowGRPO and 2× over SOTA DiffusionNFT without reward hacking.

problem: Constructing fast and accurate surrogate models for parametric PDEs from sparse, irregularly sampled observations with reliable uncertainty quantification remains challenging.
approach: Introduces Bias-Spectrum Neural Processes, a meta-learning framework integrating weak structural priors with strong physical priors via stochastic collocation and mean-field enforcement of PDE constraints.
contribution: Achieves superior accuracy and well-calibrated uncertainty quantification for nonlinear Poisson equations, Burgers dynamics, and Navier-Stokes flows in sparse-data regimes.

problem: Knowledge-intensive reasoning fails because intermediate steps are often not locally verifiable—evaluating correctness requires synthesizing clues across large external knowledge sources.
approach: Introduces Process Reward Agents, an inference-time method providing domain-grounded, step-wise rewards to frozen policies, enabling search-based decoding to rank and prune trajectories at every generation step.
contribution: Achieves 81.9% accuracy on MedQA with Qwen3-4B, state-of-the-art at 4B scale, generalizing to unseen frozen policies (0.5B-8B) with up to 25.7% accuracy improvement without policy updates.

problem: Tool-calling evaluation pipelines are highly sensitive to undocumented implementation choices, and RL training for tool-calling wastes computation during rollouts and policy updates.
approach: Systematically analyzes tool-calling evaluation sensitivity and identifies two sources of computational waste in RL-based training, proposing techniques to accelerate learning without performance degradation.
contribution: Demonstrates substantial wall-clock speedup for RL-based tool-calling training while achieving comparable performance, with systematic evaluation methodology for tool-calling benchmarks.

problem: Existing LLM-agent workflow systems rely on predefined templates and shallow matching mechanisms, limiting ability to capture deep semantic relationships and generalize to unseen tasks.
approach: Proposes GraphFlow, representing workflows as unified graphs where nodes are atomic operations, enabling adaptive workflow generation and efficient KV cache management through graph-based optimization.
contribution: Achieves approximately 4.95 percentage point average performance improvement across five benchmarks while reducing memory footprint by approximately 4× through graph-based workflow management.

problem: Existing speech enhancement diffusion models treat spectrograms as generic 2D images, ignoring intrinsic structural sparsity of audio, resulting in inefficient spectral representation and computational complexity.
approach: Proposes DVPD, a dual-view predictive diffusion model exploiting spectrograms as both visual textures and frequency-domain representations, with Frequency-Adaptive compression and Lightweight Image-based awareness modules.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art speech enhancement with only 35% parameters and 40% inference MACs compared to lightweight SOTA model PGUSE.

problem: Uncertainty quantification for LLM free-form generation relies on expensive sampling methods, limiting practical applicability.
approach: Proposes SemGrad, a gradient-based uncertainty method operating in semantic space rather than parameter space, introducing Semantic Preservation Score to identify embeddings capturing semantics, and HybridGrad combining semantic and parameter gradients.
contribution: Provides efficient and effective uncertainty estimates for free-form generation, achieving superior performance than state-of-the-art methods particularly for multiple valid responses.

problem: The spectral structure and generalization properties of trained attention layers remain poorly understood despite striking reproducible patterns like low-rank collapse and spectral outliers.
approach: Studies single-head tied-attention using random matrix theory and spin-glass theory, characterizing exact high-dimensional training/test error, interpolation thresholds, and full singular-value distribution.
contribution: Predicts full singular-value distribution of trained query-key maps including low-rank structure and outliers, and demonstrates power-law scaling laws emerge from sequential spectral recovery.

problem: Non-Markovian dynamics violate Bellman assumptions in RL, and existing work offers limited theoretical treatment of what dynamics are capturable and how to develop algorithms with optimal approximations.
approach: Introduces HodgeFlow Policy Search by interpreting TD errors as 1-cochain in topological space, decomposing into integrable and topological residual components via Bellman-de Rham projection.
contribution: Proposes algorithm achieving stability and sensitivity guarantees for RL under non-Markovian environments, significantly improving performance.

problem: Formal verification of system software with complex heap manipulations remains challenging, as automated solvers frequently fail to discharge separation logic verification conditions.
approach: Introduces SL-VC benchmark of 289 verification conditions and proposes SPLIT framework enabling predictable proof state transitions through LLM-friendly tactic library with two-stage workflow separating spatial and pure reasoning.
contribution: Demonstrates LLM-assisted proof synthesis for separation logic verification of real-world system software like LiteOS kernel and mini-gmp library.

problem: Translating natural language to optimization models suffers from silent modeling failures where incorrect formulations execute successfully but yield invalid results.
approach: Proposes Draft-and-Audit RL framework learning optimization modeling as two-step iterative workflow, optimizing policy using terminal-only verification based on execution of final audited program.
contribution: Enables models to internalize rubric-guided revision as learned capability and encourages cross-turn synergy for self-correction in NL2Opt tasks.

problem: Existing vector-based semantic typography methods lack rich semantic details and struggle to maintain structural integrity, frequently suffering from visual artifacts.
approach: Proposes VecDesigner combining Visual-Guided Score Distillation Sampling with text-related reference images, vector-based Procrustes loss for structural preservation, and positional constraints to mitigate intersections.
contribution: Outperforms existing methods in semantic expression and structural preservation, generating high-quality, expressive, and legible semantic glyphs.

problem: Developing and tuning genomic foundation models requires unifying dispersed workflows across data collection, fine-tuning, inference, benchmarking, and interpretability.
approach: Introduces Genome-Factory, a unified Python library simplifying genomic model development with automated data pipeline, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, flexible inference, multiple benchmarks, and biological interpreter via sparse auto-encoder.
contribution: Demonstrates compatibility with diverse models and fine-tuning methods, validates utility through downstream benchmarking and biological interpretation.

problem: Nonconvex constrained stochastic optimization with difference-of-convex regularization and possibly nonconvex feasible sets is challenging while maintaining feasibility and achieving favorable oracle complexity.
approach: Develops MoSSP, a momentum-based single-loop stochastic penalty method applying proximal-gradient step to Moreau envelope with polylogarithmic variants achieving O(ε^{-4}) and improved O(ε^{-3}) oracle complexity.
contribution: Provides provable complexity guarantees for finding stochastic ε-KKT points in constrained DC optimization.

problem: Subgroup discovery for survival analysis lacks effective quality functions and metrics for evaluating survival models that predict hazard functions.
approach: Introduces expected prediction entropy (EPE) metric for survival models and conditional rank statistics for subgroup quality, develops eight algorithms with main approach based on DDGroup framework.
contribution: Demonstrates recovery of ground-truth subgroups in well-specified settings and better model fit than naive Cox models, with case study on NASA jet engine data.

problem: Current LLM agents fail on the 'last mile' of commercial software automation where tools are interdependent, atomic, and prone to environmental noise.
approach: Introduces ComplexMCP benchmark with over 300 tools from 7 stateful sandboxes, seed-driven architecture simulating dynamic environments, and evaluates agents across full-context and RAG paradigms.
contribution: Reveals stark performance gap with top models failing to exceed 60% success rate versus human 90%, identifying three fundamental bottlenecks: tool retrieval saturation, over-confidence, and strategic defeatism.

problem: Circuit and sheaf discovery methods assume functions are localized to unique mechanisms, yet evidence suggests multiple distinct circuits support single tasks simultaneously.
approach: Presents empirical and theoretical evidence against Functional Anisotropy Hypothesis, introduces Overlap-Aware Sheaf Repulsion method penalizing structural overlap, and proposes Distributive Dense Circuit Hypothesis.
contribution: Demonstrates that mechanistic explanations in LLMs are inherently non-canonical with multiple, low-overlap circuit explanations, calling for rethinking how circuit discovery results should be interpreted.

problem: The maximal update parameterization (μP) enables hyperparameter transfer in supervised learning, but benefits for reinforcement learning remain unclear under non-stationary data distributions.
approach: Empirically studies CompleteP (rich) and Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) lazy parameterizations on deep RL agents, comparing hyperparameter transfer, feature consistency, and learning behavior.
contribution: Shows agents trained with CompleteP significantly improve compute and reward efficiency compared to NTK parameterization across control tasks.

problem: Traditional learning evaluations reduce learning to single aggregate test scores, obscuring per-sample generalization and how far knowledge from one example transfers to others.
approach: Introduces Generalization Spectrum evaluation framework constructing test variants arranged by transfer distance from exact recall to category-matched problems, comparing three canonical learning paradigms.
contribution: Reveals that RL converts memorization to near-transfer more efficiently than SFT, ICL exhibits strong correspondence-dependent transfer, and local improvements don't expand generalization radius.

problem: Unifying complementary strengths of diverse Vision Foundation Models into single efficient models is challenged by negative transfer inherent in monolithic distillation.
approach: Introduces PRISM, a dual-stream Mixture-of-Experts framework with two-stage paradigm: expertise deconstruction where router guides experts to specialize in distinct subspaces, then dynamic recomposition.
contribution: Establishes state-of-the-art on PASCAL-Context and NYUD-v2, validating that sparse emergent specialization effectively integrates diverse visual knowledge.

problem: Black-box prompt tuning must simultaneously address prompt interpretability and query efficiency under strict API call budgets.
approach: Proposes CRL-BPT, a curriculum reinforcement learning framework using LLM as agent to generate human-readable prompts, implementing dynamic curriculum on imitation and innovation losses with stabilization mechanisms.
contribution: Establishes state-of-the-art performance generating highly interpretable prompts under strict API call budget on reasoning and creative writing tasks.

problem: Robotic policies encounter post-training faults where retraining and system identification are impractical, requiring inference-time fault recovery.
approach: Introduces cerebellar-inspired residual control framework augmenting frozen RL policy with online corrective actions, instantiating cerebellar principles like high-dimensional pattern separation and microzone pathways.
contribution: Achieves up to +66% improvement on HalfCheetah-v5 and +53% on Humanoid-v5 under moderate faults with graceful degradation under severe shifts.

problem: Anomaly detection on tabular data is challenged by diverse anomaly types, scarce labels, and high sensitivity to hyperparameter tuning without validation labels.
approach: Proposes DVM-AD, a closed-form one-class method capturing both compactness and structure preservation through discriminant analysis, using Moore-Penrose pseudo-inverse for stability.
contribution: Achieves best average AUROC of 89.65% on 47 ADBench tabular datasets and rank 1.60 on embedding tasks, eliminating dataset-specific tuning.

problem: Automatic seizure detection from long-term EEG fails to generalize across patients and clinical settings despite reported high efficacy, indicating significant generalization gaps.
approach: Conducts large-scale empirical study evaluating 28 state-of-the-art architectures on strictly held-out dataset of 65 subjects with 4,360 hours of EEG annotated by expert neurophysiologists.
contribution: Reveals top F1 score of 32% highlighting persistent difficulty of seizure detection, identifies discordance between peak performance and population-level stability, and uncovers key failure modes.

problem: Existing RL for LLM post-training relies on uninformative binary rewards, while distillation requires costly demonstrations that don't scale.
approach: Studies natural language text feedback as intermediate signal, proposing Self Distillation training single-turn policy to match feedback-conditioned generations and Feedback Modeling predicting feedback.
contribution: Demonstrates both methods consistently outperform baselines on reasoning puzzles, competition math, and creative writing, showing potential of RL with rich multi-turn supervision at scale.

problem: Sampling algorithms for multimodal targets must remain stable as finite-dimensional approximations are refined, but Annealed Langevin Dynamics lacks uniform-in-dimension guarantees.
approach: Provides uniform-in-dimension analysis of continuous-time ALD for Gaussian-mixture targets, identifying spectral conditions linking smoothing covariance to component covariances with perturbative regime analysis.
contribution: Bridges gap between ALD empirical success and theory, establishing dimension-uniform stability under misspecified mixture score models via preconditioning.

problem: Safe RL methods using primal-dual optimization suffer from delayed constraint correction, leading to oscillatory behavior and prolonged safety violations.
approach: Proposes Constraint-Sensitive Policy Optimization incorporating local constraint sensitivity into policy updates via shortest signed distance to safety boundary.
contribution: Achieves faster safety recovery and high reward preservation on navigation and locomotion benchmarks, resulting in higher constrained returns than state-of-the-art methods.

problem: Diffusion Large Language Models suffer from high decoding cost where only small subset of tokens is decodable at each step, wasting computation on non-decodable tokens.
approach: Proposes FOCUS inference system that dynamically focuses computation on decodable tokens using attention-derived importance scores, evicting non-decodable ones to increase effective batch size.
contribution: Achieves up to 3.52× throughput improvement over production-grade LMDeploy in large-batch settings while preserving or improving generation quality.

problem: Generating mobile network topologies with directional links requires global coherence under sector, interference, connectivity, and half-duplex constraints.
approach: Introduces NetDiff, a node-conditioned denoising diffusion model for directional link topologies with Absolute Cross-Attentive Modulation providing permutation-invariant global signals.
contribution: Reaches over 95% of target performance with constant inference time, outperforms heuristic and omnidirectional baselines on graph-level metrics.

problem: Learning drifting concepts under Massart noise requires understanding complexity of online learning with changing targets and label noise.
approach: Provides computationally efficient learner achieving error η + Õ(Δ^{1/3}/γ) where η bounds noise, Δ is drift, γ is margin, with information-computation tradeoff evidence.
contribution: Shows Δ^{1/3}-scaling is unavoidable for low-degree polynomial tests even for random noise, indicating algorithm is essentially optimal.

problem: Evaluating LLM ability to generate formal program specifications is unclear since existing methods conflate proof difficulty with specification quality.
approach: Introduces Coins, a Rocq-based framework assessing specification quality by instantiating specifications on trusted test cases and generating concrete proof obligations.
contribution: Demonstrates specification generation remains formidable challenge and that test case-based formal reasoning offers more faithful and discriminative progress measure than proof-based approaches.

problem: Existing privacy canary designs for membership inference attacks are largely heuristic, lacking principled optimization to maximize detectability.
approach: Formulates canary design as bilevel optimization problem with influence function initialization and unrolled optimization with memory efficiency.
contribution: Achieves 99.6% true positive rate at 0.1% false positive rate on CIFAR-10 with optimized canaries that transfer effectively across architectures without retraining.
